label: Conveyor Belt
description: Belt conveyor with a motor and gearbox drive, idler rollers and head and tail pulleys.
general_safety: Isolate, lock out and tag out the drive and release belt tension or stored energy before any work on the conveyor.
Never reach into pinch points, rollers or pulleys while the belt is running or could start.
Keep guards in place and use an emergency pull-cord check before restarting.
general_inspection: Walk the belt line and check tracking, tension, idlers, pulleys and guards.
Check the drive motor current and temperature against the nameplate.
Check the loading and chute area for spillage, build-up or blockage.

faults.name: Belt slipping on the drive pulley
faults.reasoning: Low tension, worn pulley lagging, wet or contaminated surfaces or overloading let the belt slip on the drive pulley, causing squealing, reduced belt speed and friction heat.

triggers.symptom: Squealing noise from the drive
Reduced belt speed or throughput
Friction heat at the drive pulley
Notes mention slipping, squealing or a burning smell

inspection_steps: Compare belt speed with the drive pulley speed, or look for slip marks on the pulley and belt.
Check the belt tension at the take-up and the take-up travel remaining.
Inspect the drive pulley lagging for wear, polish or contamination.
Check the belt load against the design capacity.
maintenance_actions: Adjust the take-up to restore the correct belt tension.
Clean or replace worn or contaminated pulley lagging.
Reduce loading or improve belt wrap if slippage persists.
safety: Lock out the drive and release belt tension before touching the pulleys or take-up.
Do not use sprays or dressings on a running belt.

faults.name: Belt mistracking
faults.reasoning: A belt running off-centre rubs the structure, spills material and wears the edge. Causes include misaligned idlers or pulleys, uneven loading and material build-up.

triggers.symptom: Notes mention the belt drifting, rubbing or spilling
Raised vibration
Unusual noise, possibly the belt edge rubbing the frame
Spillage or reduced throughput

inspection_steps: Walk the belt and note where it drifts and on which side.
Check idler and pulley alignment, squareness to the belt centreline and frame level.
Check for material build-up on rollers, pulleys or the return side.
Check the loading point: is the material landing off-centre?
maintenance_actions: Adjust or re-square the idlers and pulleys that cause the drift.
Clean build-up from rollers and pulleys.
Centre the load at the chute and fit or adjust tracking idlers if needed.
safety: Never adjust idlers while the belt is running.
Lock out the drive before reaching near the pulleys or return rollers.

faults.name: Idler or roller bearing failure
faults.reasoning: A seized or failing idler bearing makes grinding or squealing noise, raises roller temperature and can wear a flat on the roller or damage the belt.

triggers.symptom: Grinding, squealing or rattling from the rollers
Unusual noise
High temperature at a roller (70 °C or more)
Raised vibration
Notes mention rollers, idlers or bearings

inspection_steps: Walk the line and listen for the noisy roller; check which idler runs hot with an infrared thermometer.
Check by hand (conveyor locked out) that each suspect roller turns freely.
Look for flat spots, damaged shells and missing rollers.
Check for material build-up around the roller ends.
maintenance_actions: Replace missing or damaged rollers and check the neighbouring ones.
Add idler inspection and replacement to the regular maintenance route.
safety: Never touch a roller while the belt is running; it can trap clothing or hands.
Let hot rollers cool and lock out the conveyor before replacing them.

faults.name: Drive motor overload
faults.reasoning: A heavy, jammed or badly loaded belt makes the drive motor draw extra current and run hot, sometimes tripping its protection.

triggers.symptom: Motor temperature is high (80 °C or more)
Motor temperature is very high (90 °C or more)
Low vibration points away from a mechanical fault
Reduced performance under load
Humming from the motor
Notes mention overload, tripping or jamming

inspection_steps: Measure motor current and compare with the nameplate.
Check the belt load, chute and transfer points for blockage or overfeeding.
Check for seized rollers or a dragging belt that adds resistance.
Check motor ventilation and the thermal protection settings.
maintenance_actions: Reduce the feed rate or clear the blockage.
Free or replace seized rollers that are adding drag.
Review motor and gearbox sizing if the load is above design.
safety: Lock out the drive and release the belt tension before clearing a jam.
Do not reset a tripped motor repeatedly without finding the cause.

faults.name: Belt wear, damage or loss of tension
faults.reasoning: A worn, stretched or damaged belt loses grip and throughput and can wander or sag between idlers.

triggers.symptom: Reduced throughput
Squealing or unusual noise
Raised vibration
Notes mention wear, cracks, stretch or sag

inspection_steps: Inspect the belt surface, edges and splices for cuts, fraying and cracks.
Check belt sag between idlers and the take-up travel remaining.
Measure belt thickness against the original specification.
Check the splices for separation.
maintenance_actions: Repair or re-splice the damaged section.
Re-tension the belt or shorten it if the take-up is out of travel.
Plan belt replacement if wear is widespread.
safety: Lock out the drive and block the belt against movement before splicing or repair.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling frayed belt or steel cord.

faults.name: Drive gearbox / reducer fault
faults.reasoning: A worn or under-lubricated reducer makes whining or grinding noise, runs hot and may leak oil.

triggers.symptom: Whining or grinding from the gearbox
Oil leakage at the gearbox
High gearbox temperature (80 °C or more)
Raised vibration
Notes mention the gearbox, oil or leaks

inspection_steps: Check the gearbox oil level, colour and smell, and look for metal particles.
Check the seals, covers and breather for leaks.
Compare gearbox temperature with the motor and with previous readings.
Check the coupling and the torque arm or mounting.
maintenance_actions: Top up or change the oil with the specified grade.
Replace leaking seals and clear the breather.
Plan an overhaul or replacement if the gears or bearings are worn.
safety: Lock out the drive and release belt tension before opening the gearbox.
Let hot oil cool before draining or sampling.
